rationale: M60 R10 sibling pin. csharp builds an override endpoint the same way java does (`${ownerFqn}.${name}${signature}`), so the parameter list is inside the string the edge label is derived from. Its pre-fix rule cut at the FIRST '(' before splitting on dots — which is the honest answer for these shapes, but truncates a paren-bearing owner chain — and the two lanes now call one shared rule (src/ast/override-context.ts localEdgeLabel). What this fixture catches is the OTHER direction: if csharp ever adopted java's pre-fix derivation (split on '.', last two segments, cut each at '('), the qualified parameter type inside the signature would be split as a qualifier and the labels would become `Text.StringBuilder,bool)` and `Generic.KeyValuePair<string, bool>)`, measured below as the forbids. Parameter types are written QUALIFIED on purpose — the signature carries the written text — and the base method is abstract with an explicit `override` because that, not interface implementation, is what this lane resolves overrides from (measured: an interface-only shape emits zero override edges).

forbidRelationships.note: what java's pre-fix derivation produces on this signature (`System.Text.StringBuilder` splits as a qualifier): not a name, owner lost
